items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The first time I ever heard Mary Lou Williams, she was billed as the lady who swings the band and she was just that. She was one of the swingiest pianists I had ever heard play in any kind of band.

ctx.x: The Howard Theater looms large in the musical culture of Washington D.C. Can you share some of your recollections about the Howard Theater?

My grandfather’s church was the Florida Avenue Baptist Church and if you came out the front door and went slightly to the left you walked right into the front door of the Howard Theater. If you went a little further, then a left you went around to the stage door. And my father’s office was on S Street. Howard is on T Street and on S Street… 7th Street and S Street was my father’s office so I had an entrée. The guy that was the… Shep Allen who was the manager of the theater was a good friend of my family and sort…

The Jimmy Lunsford band came to Washington D.C. the first time and I remember a whole bunch of us had heard about this band of young people. All the girls went nuts because these were a bunch of handsome fellows, immaculately dressed, sang and played better then most of the older guys. The visual aspects of the music were at that time as exciting to me as the oral aspects because you saw… even as a young guy I realized that you react to what you see before you react to what you hear because the lights go up and…

items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: I was alternating with Billy Taylor... So I told Billy Taylor, 'Billy, came over and play this set.'

ctx.x: I don't know what happened because see I was working on the East Side and various places out of the city, but when I got this job I was alternating with Billy Taylor. I can't remember the name of this place, at 52nd and Eighth Avenue. So I had a way of always helping musicians. At one time I was recording for Moe Asch and what happened, he was expecting a pianist and I had taken Bill Coleman and Al Hail with me and he got a little peeved about it but he recorded it, because they were out of work and I put them…
